body: I personally think it would make sense to change the second WPT test to align with chrome/webkit where `window.location.href === orig_location` without the hash. With the change in the spec being to make the location hash setter to consider empty fragment and null fragment the same (and early return without navigation). This would match as I understand 2 of 3 browser engine's behavior.

I agree with the desire to move toward 2/3 browser behavior.

IIUC that would involve:

- Changing the spec to treat null and empty string fragments as the same, for the purposes of this no-op step
- Updating the second WPT

Such PRs would be welcome!

> I personally think it would make sense to change the second WPT test to align with chrome/webkit where window.location.href === orig_location without the hash. With the change in the spec being to make the location hash setter to consider empty fragment and null fragment the same (and early return without navigation). This would match as I understand 2 of 3 browser engine's behavior.

@shannonbooth - How does Firefox's treat `location.hash = ""` or `location.hash = null` differently from Chrome and Safari?

In Firefox 137, Chrome 135, and Safari 18.3.1:

1. If I load https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HTML#History
2. And set `location.hash = ""` in the dev tools console,
3. The URL changes to `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HTML#`

And:

1. If I load https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HTML#History
2. And set `location.hash = null` (no quotes) in the dev tools console,
3. The URL changes to `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HTML#null`

With the change in the spec being to make the location hash setter to consider empty fragment and null fragment the same (and early return without navigation). > [@shannonbooth](https://github.com/shannonbooth?rgh-link-date=2025-04-25T06%3A43%3A07.000Z) - How does Firefox's treat `location.hash = ""` or `location.hash = null` differently from Chrome and Safari?
> 
> In Firefox 137, Chrome 135, and Safari 18.3.1:
> 
> 1. If I load [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HTML#History](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HTML#History)
> 2. And set `location.hash = ""` in the dev tools console,
> 3. The URL changes to `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HTML#`
> 
> And:
> 
> 1. If I load [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HTML#History](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HTML#History)
> 2. And set `location.hash = null` (no quotes) in the dev tools console,
> 3. The URL changes to `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HTML#null`

Right, both examples also work the same way in Ladybird (which I hack on in my spare time).

The difference with Firefox is if you navigate to a URL _without_ a fragment and then set it to the empty string. As an example:

- Load `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HTML`
- Set `location.hash = ""` in dev tools console
- The URL in Firefox changes to `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HTML#` instead of what Chrome and WebKit do of skipping the navigation entirely, and leaving the URL as: `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HTML`

The behavior is tested by this WPT test: https://wpt.live/html/browsers/history/the-location-interface/location_hash_set_empty_string.html
